correctness.rationale: Reduction splits by constants, and the additive reduction kernel is sl₂(k) because 2 is invertible. Involutions in the residue group are exactly the nonsingular trace-zero projective lines: Cayley–Hamilton proves both directions. The singular locus x²+yz=0 has q+1 projective points (q with y=1, one with y=0), leaving q² involutions. The split ones correspond to unordered pairs of projective-line fixed points. The plus part of the projective centralizer is k[A]×/k×, cyclic of size q−1 or q+1; an eigenspace swap or field conjugation gives the reversing involution, yielding the stated dihedral centralizer and other-involution count, also at q=3. Every lift of exact order two has additive part in the two-dimensional −1 eigenspace. Equal-base lifts commute only when equal. For distinct commuting residue involutions, projective commutation forces anticommutation of the trace-zero representatives A,B, so A,B,AB form the three different simultaneous character lines of the adjoint action. The lift commutation condition matches exactly the AB coefficients, giving q disjoint K_(q,q)'s and exactly q neighbors per commuting fiber. Counting residue pairs and diagonals gives q⁶; the stated degrees and edge counts follow. The reduction kernel has odd order and the residue dihedral centralizers rule out elementary abelian 2-rank three. Thus the product is the unique common neighbor of each commuting pair. Each fixed ordered generating pair of a residue Klein four has q³ commuting lift pairs, one per lifted subgroup. The frozen q=3,5 checker was inspected, not run; those cases do not establish the arbitrary prime-power statement.

value.rationale: Commuting involution graphs are standard group invariants; split dual numbers give a natural first nontrivial congruence extension. The classification gives the local relation above each edge, including complete components, independent fibers and unique triangles. That is more informative than the aggregate count q⁶ or an extrapolation from two small fields and is useful when comparing which features of a residue graph survive congruence lifting. No global isomorphism classification or extension to other rings is asserted.
